title: Competing primary CTAs
summary: The hero presents two equally weighted CTAs (SHOP MEN and SHOP WOMEN) that split user intent and delay the path to a single product or category, reducing the clarity of the primary action.
problem: The hero presents two equally prominent CTAs (SHOP MEN and SHOP WOMEN) that split user intent and delay the path to a single product or category, reducing the clarity of the primary action.
recommended_change: h1: Wildly Comfortable. Super Natural.; cta: SHOP BESTSELLERS; notes: Replace the two CTAs with a single, high-intent CTA that leads to a curated bestseller collection, reducing choice overload and focusing the user on a single next step.
evidence: Hero section contains both 'SHOP MEN' and 'SHOP WOMEN' as primary CTAs, with no single dominant CTA; the page also shows 'Shop All' in the nav and 'Shop + -' in the cart drawer, creating multiple competing paths. | H1: 'Wildly Comfortable. Super Natural.' CTAs: 'SHOP MEN' and 'SHOP WOMEN' with no subheadline to clarify the brand's unique selling proposition.
opportunity_basis: 2,160,000 annual visits x 2.10% conversion x 2.0-8.0% relative lift x $78 order value
